## Claims
### claim-000
evidenceId: live-web-0

Employment — reference for decision research. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristics that affect how quickly a career switch can happen. Affects whether timing favors acting now versus deferring.
### claim-001

## Options (human chooses — no automatic recommendation)
### opt-change-career: Change career path now (staged transition)
supporting_evidence: live-web-0, live-web-1, live-web-2
advantages: Supporting signal: Employment — reference for decision research. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristics that affect how quickly a career; Can start with a staged move rather than an all-or-nothing jump; May improve long-term optionality if demand signals hold
risks: Income discontinuity during transition; Market timing or hiring-cycle mismatch; Skills gap versus target role requirements
unknowns: Target role compensation range in Japan for your profile; How portable current skills are to the destination path; Personal runway and household constraints
### opt-stay-or-defer: Stay / defer change and gather stronger evidence first
supporting_evidence: live-web-0, live-web-1, live-web-2
advantages: Preserves current income stability while researching; Allows targeted upskilling before committing; Can validate weak spots such as: Employment discrimination — reference for decision research. Japan employment and mobility have structural characteristi
risks: Opportunity cost if the window for switching narrows; Staying too long in a declining fit
unknowns: How long to defer before a hard go/no-go date; Whether internal mobility is a better bridge than an external switch
